headline: Medium-risk shared-state and output-chaining between Dify and Great Expectations can leak data or cascade errors; no direct prompt-injection channel is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dify can ingest tool outputs and files, but Great Expectations is documented as file-based validation with no direct interactive channel. The pair lacks a documented shared clipboard/MCP bridge, so prompt injection is possible only through manual or file-mediated handoff, not by default. Uncertainty remains because Dify has broad network and file access while GE reads/writes validation artifacts.
conditions: IF an operator copies Great Expectations validation text into a Dify prompt or knowledge file, injection becomes plausible.
IF both agents are wired to the same shared folder without content filtering, file-mediated injection is possible.
mitigations: Keep GE outputs in a separate folder from Dify inputs.
Require manual review before pasting validation text into Dify.
Strip instructions from validation reports before ingestion.
Disable any automatic file-sync between the two systems.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to shared artifacts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Dify explicitly touches conversation logs, knowledge base content, and secrets, while Great Expectations touches data sources, validation results, and documentation. If they share a workspace or files, sensitive data can flow from Dify into GE artifacts or vice versa. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default file-centric workflows, though not proven by direct evidence.
conditions: IF Dify conversation logs or knowledge-base files are placed in a shared directory, GE can read them as validation inputs.
IF GE validation results are imported back into Dify, sensitive source data may be exposed in prompts or logs.
mitigations: Use separate directories for Dify and GE artifacts.
Exclude conversation logs from GE scans.
Redact secrets before exporting files to GE.
Limit Dify knowledge-base uploads to non-sensitive documents.
requires-engineering: enforce per-tool access controls on shared storage.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Dify can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses; Great Expectations can install packages and operate on files. If both are pointed at the same mutable workspace, they can overwrite each other's artifacts or create inconsistent validation state. The conflict is not guaranteed, but overlapping file writes are enough to make the pathway real.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same project directory, file clobbering or stale-state bugs can occur.
IF GE installs packages in an environment Dify also uses, dependency drift can break workflows.
mitigations: Assign each agent its own working directory.
Pin dependencies in a lockfile.
Run GE in a disposable virtual environment.
Avoid concurrent writes to shared artifacts.
requires-engineering: add file locks around shared outputs.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dify can generate workflow outputs and Great Expectations can consume files as validation inputs, so B may treat A's artifacts as authoritative without an explicit verification step. Great Expectations is a validator, which reduces but does not eliminate the risk that bad Dify-generated content propagates into downstream decisions or reports. The interaction is inferred from file-based workflows, not directly documented.
conditions: IF GE is configured to validate Dify-generated files without human review, erroneous upstream content can cascade into reports.
IF Dify outputs are used as source-of-truth inputs for GE tests, false assumptions can propagate.
mitigations: Insert a human review step before GE consumes Dify outputs.
Validate schemas before content-based checks.
Keep Dify-generated artifacts labeled as untrusted.
Compare GE results against an independent source.
requires-engineering: add automated provenance verification.

E_compliance.rationale: Dify handles conversation logs, knowledge-base content, and secrets, while Great Expectations handles validation results and documentation. No residency or certification mismatch is documented, so only a limited compliance gap is visible: if regulated data is moved from Dify into GE artifacts, retention and logging policies may diverge. The other agent is cited because the risk is pairwise through shared data handling.
conditions: IF regulated data from Dify is exported into GE validation files, retention controls may differ across systems.
IF Dify secrets appear in GE logs or documentation, compliance handling becomes inconsistent.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of GE documentation outputs.
Redact secrets before exporting from Dify.
Set short retention on shared validation artifacts.
Document which system is system-of-record for each data class.
requires-engineering: align retention policies across both tools.
